idiom_name: Monitor / MonitorMixin (synchronize, new_cond) - a core class bundling a reentrant lock with condition variables
implementation_notes: Ruby ships the pattern: require 'monitor' (a core class since Ruby 3.1) provides Monitor, a reentrant lock whose synchronize block is the synchronized method, and Monitor#new_cond returns a MonitorMixin::ConditionVariable whose wait must be called inside synchronize and whose signal/broadcast wake the waiters; MonitorMixin mixes the same behaviour into any class so its instance methods can synchronise. The lower level - Thread::Mutex plus Thread::ConditionVariable - is available for hand-written monitors, and Thread::Queue is the ready-made producer/consumer handoff. The GVL means only one thread executes Ruby code at a time, but blocking I/O and C extensions release it, so the monitor is still required whenever an invariant spans more than one statement.
pitfalls: Monitor#synchronize is reentrant, but MonitorMixin::ConditionVariable#wait must be called inside it (otherwise ThreadError) and may wake spuriously, so the predicate loop is mandatory.
Thread::Mutex is not reentrant, unlike Monitor: mixing the two on the same object, or calling into another locked object from inside synchronize, causes self-deadlock.
The GVL does not make an object thread-safe - invariants that span several statements still need synchronize - and doing I/O while holding the monitor serialises unrelated callers.
